answer_text:
Let \(f=\mathbf 1_E\). Since \(E\subset[0,2\pi]\) is measurable, \(f\in L^1([0,2\pi])\).

By the Riemann–Lebesgue lemma,
\[
\int_E e^{inx}\,dx=\int_0^{2\pi} \mathbf 1_E(x)e^{inx}\,dx \to 0
\qquad (n\to\infty).
\]

Now
\[
\int_E \cos(nx+t_n)\,dx
=\Re\left(\int_E e^{i(nx+t_n)}\,dx\right)
=\Re\left(e^{it_n}\int_E e^{inx}\,dx\right).
\]
Hence
\[
\left|\int_E \cos(nx+t_n)\,dx\right|
\le 
\left|\int_E e^{inx}\,dx\right|
\to 0.
\]

Thus the limit is always \(0\), for every real sequence \((t_n)\).

\[
\boxed{0}
\]
